requirements.source_text: These controls have been developed after taking into consideration the cybersecurity needs of organizations and sectors in the kingdom. Every organization within the scope of these controls must comply with all applicable controls in this document.
requirements.source_summary: The organization should determine which DCC controls apply to its operations, data, and scope, and maintain an accountable process for implementing all applicable controls.

todo.name: Determine and implement applicable DCC controls
todo.description: Perform and document a DCC applicability assessment, assign control owners, address identified gaps, and maintain an implementation plan covering every applicable control.

policies.name: Data Cybersecurity Governance Policy
policies.description: Define the organization’s approach to identifying, implementing, monitoring, and maintaining applicable data cybersecurity controls.

policies.name: Control Applicability and Compliance Policy
policies.description: Establish criteria and responsibilities for determining control applicability and documenting any approved justification for controls that are not applicable.

documents.name: DCC Applicability Assessment
documents.description: A documented assessment mapping organizational activities, systems, and data to applicable DCC controls.

documents.name: DCC Compliance Implementation Plan
documents.description: A plan listing applicable controls, owners, target dates, implementation status, and remediation actions.

documents.name: Control Ownership Register
documents.description: A register identifying accountable and responsible owners for each applicable control.

evidence.name: Completed DCC applicability assessment
evidence.description: Approved assessment showing the basis for determining which controls apply.

evidence.name: Control implementation tracker
evidence.description: Current tracker showing control status, assigned owners, open gaps, and remediation progress.

evidence.name: Management approval or review records
evidence.description: Meeting minutes, approvals, or attestations demonstrating oversight of the DCC compliance program.

requirements.source_text: In order tocomply with item 3 of article 10 of NCA’s mandate and as per the Royal Decree number (57231) dated 10/11/1439H, all organizations within the scope of these controls must implement whatever necessary to ensure continuous compliance with the controls, which cannot be achieved without achieving continuous compliance with the Essential Cybersecurity Controls (ECC –1: 2018) where applicable. NCA evaluates organizations’ compliance with the DCC through multiple means such as self-assessments by the organizations, and/or external assessments, in accordance with the mechanisms deemed appropriate by NCA.
requirements.source_summary: The organization should maintain continuous compliance with applicable DCC requirements, including applicable ECC requirements, and be prepared to support compliance evaluations using the mechanisms specified by NCA.

todo.name: Establish continuous DCC compliance monitoring
todo.description: Implement an ongoing compliance program that tracks applicable DCC and ECC obligations, monitors control performance, manages remediation, and preserves materials needed for self-assessments or external assessments.

policies.name: Continuous Compliance Monitoring Policy
policies.description: Define recurring compliance monitoring, control testing, issue escalation, remediation tracking, and reporting responsibilities.

policies.name: Cybersecurity Assessment Policy
policies.description: Set requirements for preparing, conducting, approving, and retaining self-assessments and third-party assessments.

documents.name: DCC/ECC Compliance Calendar
documents.description: A calendar of recurring control reviews, assessments, evidence collection, reporting, and remediation activities.

documents.name: Compliance Issue and Remediation Register
documents.description: A register of findings, risk ratings, responsible owners, corrective actions, due dates, and closure approvals.

documents.name: Assessment Readiness Plan
documents.description: A plan identifying assessment scope, evidence owners, repositories, testing activities, and response procedures.

evidence.name: Completed self-assessment results
evidence.description: Approved self-assessment records showing control evaluation results and identified gaps.

evidence.name: External assessment reports
evidence.description: Assessment reports, management responses, and remediation plans where an external assessment has been performed.

evidence.name: Periodic compliance dashboards
evidence.description: Management reports showing control status, overdue actions, recurring monitoring results, and compliance trends.

requirements.source_text: 1-1-1With reference to ECC control 1-8-1, the cybersecurity function in the organization must review the implementation of the Data Cybersecurity Controls periodically as specified for each data classification level.At least annually
requirements.source_summary: The cybersecurity function should periodically review implementation of the DCC controls according to the review interval associated with each data classification level, including an annual minimum interval where applicable.

todo.name: Conduct periodic DCC implementation reviews
todo.description: Create a review schedule based on data classification, assess implementation of relevant DCC controls, record results and deficiencies, and obtain cybersecurity function sign-off.

policies.name: DCC Control Review Policy
policies.description: Define review frequency by data classification, review scope, responsibilities, testing methods, issue escalation, and approval requirements.

documents.name: DCC Review Schedule
documents.description: A schedule linking data classification levels and covered controls to required review dates and responsible reviewers.

documents.name: DCC Control Review Checklist
documents.description: A checklist for evaluating implementation, operating effectiveness, exceptions, and remediation status.

documents.name: Control Review Findings Register
documents.description: A record of review findings, risk assessments, corrective actions, owners, and closure evidence.

evidence.name: Completed periodic review reports
evidence.description: Signed reports showing the controls reviewed, classification scope, review date, results, and identified gaps.

evidence.name: Review meeting records
evidence.description: Cybersecurity function meeting minutes or approvals confirming review completion and follow-up actions.

evidence.name: Remediation closure evidence
evidence.description: Records demonstrating that deficiencies identified during reviews were corrected or formally tracked.

requirements.source_text: 1-2-1-1Screening andvetting candidates injobsrelated to data handling.
requirements.source_summary: The organization should apply screening and vetting to candidates for jobs involving data handling, with the process aligned to the sensitivity of the role and information handled.

todo.name: Screen candidates for data-handling roles
todo.description: Identify roles involving data handling, define appropriate screening and vetting steps, complete them before access or appointment as applicable, and retain completion records.

policies.name: Personnel Screening and Vetting Policy
policies.description: Define screening requirements, approval responsibilities, confidentiality safeguards, exceptions, and record-retention practices for data-handling roles.

policies.name: Data-Handling Role Access Policy
policies.description: Require confirmation of role screening status before granting access to data or data-handling systems.

documents.name: Data-Handling Role Register
documents.description: An inventory of positions that involve handling or access to organizational data.

documents.name: Candidate Screening Procedure
documents.description: A procedure describing screening steps, decision criteria, approvals, and escalation of adverse results.

documents.name: Personnel Screening Record
documents.description: A controlled record showing screening status, completion date, reviewer, and any approved restrictions.

evidence.name: Completed screening records
evidence.description: Personnel or recruitment records demonstrating that candidates for applicable roles were screened and vetted.

evidence.name: Role classification records
evidence.description: Approved job descriptions or role assessments identifying positions that involve data handling.

evidence.name: Access approval dependencies
evidence.description: Workflow records showing that screening status was checked before relevant access was approved.

requirements.source_text: 2-1-1-1Strict restriction toallow only the minimum number of personnel accessing, viewingand sharingdata based on lists of privileges limited to Saudi-national employees unless exempted bythe Authorizing Official(the head of the organization or his/her delegate) and those lists are approved by the Authorizing Official.
requirements.source_summary: Access to view, share, and handle data should be limited to the minimum necessary personnel through approved privilege lists, with the specified national-employee condition and authorization process managed by the Authorizing Official.

todo.name: Restrict and approve data access privileges
todo.description: Identify the minimum personnel requiring access, maintain privilege lists reflecting the applicable national-employee condition, document authorized exemptions, and obtain Authorizing Official approval before granting or retaining access.

policies.name: Data Access Control Policy
policies.description: Define least-privilege access, approved personnel eligibility, exemption handling, authorization, provisioning, review, and removal requirements.

policies.name: Authorizing Official Delegation Policy
policies.description: Define the Authorizing Official’s approval authority and any documented delegation for data access decisions.

documents.name: Approved Data Privilege List
documents.description: A controlled list of personnel authorized to view, share, or handle specified data, including access scope and approval status.

documents.name: Data Access Request and Approval Form
documents.description: A form capturing business justification, required privileges, personnel eligibility, exemption details where applicable, and Authorizing Official approval.

documents.name: Data Access Matrix
documents.description: A mapping of data sets and systems to approved roles and individual privileges.

evidence.name: Approved privilege lists
evidence.description: Current, version-controlled lists showing the minimum authorized personnel and required approvals.

evidence.name: Access request records
evidence.description: Completed requests demonstrating documented justification and Authorizing Official approval.

evidence.name: System access reports
evidence.description: System-generated reports comparing actual data access with approved privilege lists.

evidence.name: Approved exemption records
evidence.description: Documented Authorizing Official approvals for applicable exceptions.

requirements.source_text: 2-1-1-2Prohibiting the sharing of approved lists of privileges with unauthorized persons.
requirements.source_summary: Approved data-access privilege lists should be protected from disclosure to unauthorized persons through controlled handling and distribution.

todo.name: Protect approved privilege lists
todo.description: Classify and store privilege lists in a restricted repository, limit access to authorized personnel, control copying and distribution, and investigate any suspected unauthorized disclosure.

policies.name: Access List Protection Policy
policies.description: Define handling, storage, distribution, confidentiality, and disposal requirements for approved privilege lists.

policies.name: Sensitive Information Handling Policy
policies.description: Establish safeguards for documents containing access information and procedures for reporting suspected unauthorized sharing.

documents.name: Privilege List Distribution Register
documents.description: A record of authorized recipients, distribution dates, approved channels, and acknowledgements.

documents.name: Restricted Repository Access Register
documents.description: A register of users authorized to access the repository containing privilege lists.

documents.name: Privilege List Handling Procedure
documents.description: A procedure covering creation, approval, storage, transmission, version control, and secure disposal.

evidence.name: Repository access logs
evidence.description: Logs showing access to privilege lists by authorized users.

evidence.name: Distribution and acknowledgement records
evidence.description: Records confirming controlled distribution and recipient acknowledgement of handling obligations.

evidence.name: Document permissions and configuration evidence
evidence.description: Screenshots or configuration exports demonstrating restricted access and controlled sharing settings.

evidence.name: Incident records where applicable
evidence.description: Investigation and response records for suspected unauthorized disclosure.

requirements.source_text: 2-1-2Managing identities and access rights to view data using Privileged Access Management systems.
requirements.source_summary: Privileged Access Management should be used to manage identities and access rights for viewing data, including privileged identities and their associated permissions.

todo.name: Manage data access through PAM
todo.description: Identify privileged identities and data-viewing access paths, onboard them to an approved PAM solution, enforce controlled access workflows, and monitor privileged activity.

policies.name: Privileged Access Management Policy
policies.description: Define privileged account ownership, approval, credential protection, session control, monitoring, emergency access, and periodic review.

policies.name: Identity and Access Management Policy
policies.description: Establish identity lifecycle, authentication, authorization, and access removal requirements for data environments.

documents.name: PAM Architecture and Scope Document
documents.description: A document identifying systems, privileged accounts, data environments, and access paths covered by PAM.

documents.name: Privileged Account Inventory
documents.description: An inventory of privileged identities, owners, associated systems, privilege levels, and status.

documents.name: PAM Operating Procedure
documents.description: Procedures for requesting, approving, provisioning, using, monitoring, and revoking privileged access.

evidence.name: PAM configuration exports
evidence.description: Configuration evidence showing enrolled systems, accounts, approval workflows, and access controls.

evidence.name: Privileged session logs
evidence.description: Records of privileged access sessions, including identity, time, target system, and activity where captured.

evidence.name: Privileged access approval records
evidence.description: Approved requests demonstrating that access was authorized before use.

evidence.name: PAM access review reports
evidence.description: Reports showing periodic reconciliation of PAM identities and permissions with approved access.

requirements.source_text: 2-1-3In addition to ECC subcontrol 2-2-3-5,the approved lists of privilegesand privileges used to handle data must be reviewedas specified for each data classification level.At least annuallyAt least every 3 months
requirements.source_summary: Approved privilege lists and privileges used to handle data should be reviewed at the interval associated with each data classification level, including annual or more frequent review intervals where applicable.

todo.name: Review data privileges on the required schedule
todo.description: Map each data environment to its classification, schedule reviews at the applicable interval, reconcile approved lists and actual privileges, remove unnecessary access, and document approvals and exceptions.

policies.name: Data Privilege Review Policy
policies.description: Define review frequency by data classification, reviewer responsibilities, reconciliation methods, access-removal timelines, and approval requirements.

documents.name: Privilege Review Calendar
documents.description: A calendar showing required annual or more frequent reviews based on data classification.

documents.name: Access Reconciliation Checklist
documents.description: A checklist for comparing approved privilege lists, PAM records, application permissions, and current personnel status.

documents.name: Privilege Review and Exception Register
documents.description: A record of review outcomes, retained access justifications, removals, exceptions, owners, and approvals.

evidence.name: Completed privilege review attestations
evidence.description: Signed reviews confirming that approved lists and actual data-handling privileges were examined.

evidence.name: Access reconciliation reports
evidence.description: Reports identifying matches, excessive privileges, inactive users, and corrective actions.

evidence.name: Access removal records
evidence.description: Tickets or system logs demonstrating removal or modification of unnecessary privileges.

evidence.name: Review schedule compliance report
evidence.description: A report showing completion of reviews within the intervals applicable to each classification level.

requirements.source_text: 2-2-1-1Applying security patches and updates from the time of announcement onsystems used to handle data as specified for each data classification level.At least everymonthImmediately
requirements.source_summary: Systems used to handle data should receive security patches and updates within the timing applicable to the relevant data classification level, including immediate handling where specified.

todo.name: Apply security patches to data-handling systems
todo.description: Maintain an inventory of systems handling data, monitor patch announcements, assess applicability and risk, deploy patches within the classification-based time limits, and document approved exceptions or compensating actions.

policies.name: Vulnerability and Patch Management Policy
policies.description: Define patch identification, risk assessment, testing, deployment, emergency handling, verification, exception approval, and reporting requirements.

policies.name: Change Management Policy
policies.description: Require controlled authorization, testing, implementation, and rollback planning for security updates.

documents.name: Data-Handling System Inventory
documents.description: An inventory identifying systems that handle data, their classifications, owners, technologies, and patching responsibilities.

documents.name: Patch Management Procedure
documents.description: A procedure for receiving announcements, assessing updates, prioritizing deployment, validating installation, and handling failures.

documents.name: Patch Exception Register
documents.description: A record of deferred patches, reasons, risk acceptance, compensating controls, owners, and target dates.

evidence.name: Patch deployment reports
evidence.description: System or endpoint management reports showing patch versions, deployment dates, and affected assets.

evidence.name: Patch announcement and assessment records
evidence.description: Records showing when relevant patches were identified and how applicability and urgency were assessed.

evidence.name: Vulnerability scan results
evidence.description: Scan reports demonstrating remediation of relevant missing patches.

evidence.name: Approved exception records
evidence.description: Authorizations and compensating-control evidence for patches not deployed within the applicable timeframe.

requirements.source_text: 3-1-1-1Screening orvetting third-party employees who have access to the data.
requirements.source_summary: Third-party employees who have access to organizational data should undergo screening or vetting appropriate to their data-access role before or as a condition of access.

todo.name: Vet third-party personnel with data access
todo.description: Identify third-party personnel requiring data access, define screening or vetting prerequisites in contractual and onboarding workflows, verify completion, and prevent or remove access when requirements are not met.

policies.name: Third-Party Personnel Security Policy
policies.description: Define screening, vetting, approval, monitoring, and access-removal requirements for external personnel with data access.

policies.name: Third-Party Risk Management Policy
policies.description: Require security due diligence and contractual controls for suppliers and service providers handling organizational data.

documents.name: Third-Party Data Access Register
documents.description: A register of external personnel with data access, sponsoring supplier, role, systems, data scope, and access status.

documents.name: Third-Party Security Requirements
documents.description: Contractual or onboarding requirements covering screening, confidentiality, access restrictions, and notification obligations.

documents.name: Third-Party Vetting Verification Form
documents.description: A controlled form recording vetting status, verification source, completion date, reviewer, and any restrictions.

evidence.name: Third-party screening or vetting records
evidence.description: Records demonstrating completed screening or vetting for external personnel with data access.

evidence.name: Supplier due-diligence files
evidence.description: Approved assessments and supporting documentation for suppliers whose personnel access data.

evidence.name: Contractual security clauses
evidence.description: Executed agreements containing applicable personnel screening, confidentiality, and data-access obligations.

evidence.name: Third-party access approval and removal records
evidence.description: Workflow or ticket records showing access was granted only after verification and removed when no longer justified.

requirements.source_text: 3-1-1-2Requiring contractual commitment by third-partiesto securely dispose the organization’s data at the end of the contract or in case of contract termination, including providing evidences of such disposal to the organization.
requirements.source_summary: Third-party contracts must address secure disposal of the organization’s data when the contract ends or is terminated, with disposal evidence provided to the organization.

todo.name: Implement third-party data disposal obligations
todo.description: Update third-party agreements and offboarding processes to require secure disposal of organizational data at contract completion or termination, define acceptable evidence, and assign responsibility for collecting and reviewing that evidence.

policies.name: Third-Party Data Management Policy
policies.description: Define requirements for third-party data handling, return, retention, and secure disposal at the end of a contractual relationship.

policies.name: Third-Party Offboarding Policy
policies.description: Establish steps for confirming data return or disposal, revoking access, and closing third-party services when contracts end or are terminated.

documents.name: Third-Party Contract Security Addendum
documents.description: Contract language specifying secure data disposal obligations, timing, scope, evidence requirements, and any applicable exceptions.

documents.name: Third-Party Data Disposal Procedure
documents.description: Procedure for identifying data held by a third party, initiating disposal, obtaining evidence, and recording completion.

documents.name: Third-Party Data Inventory
documents.description: Inventory identifying organizational data shared with or held by each third party to support complete disposal verification.

documents.name: Data Disposal Certificate Template
documents.description: Standard form for third parties to confirm what data was disposed of, when, how, and by whom.

evidence.name: Executed contracts and security addenda
evidence.description: Agreements containing the required third-party data disposal commitment.

evidence.name: Completed disposal certificates or equivalent confirmations
evidence.description: Third-party evidence showing that organizational data was securely disposed of after contract completion or termination.

evidence.name: Contract termination and offboarding records
evidence.description: Records showing that data disposal was initiated, reviewed, and closed as part of third-party offboarding.

evidence.name: Data inventory reconciliation
evidence.description: Records demonstrating that identified data held by the third party was addressed during disposal verification.

requirements.source_text: 3-1-1-3Documentingall data sharing operations within third-parties, including data sharing justification.
requirements.source_summary: Data-sharing activities involving third parties must be documented, including the justification for each sharing activity.

todo.name: Establish a third-party data-sharing record
todo.description: Create and maintain a centralized register of data-sharing operations with third parties, recording the data involved, recipient, purpose, scope, timing, and business or operational justification.

policies.name: Third-Party Data Sharing Policy
policies.description: Define how data-sharing activities with third parties are requested, justified, approved, documented, reviewed, and closed.

policies.name: Data Governance Policy
policies.description: Set ownership and accountability for maintaining records of data-sharing operations and their stated justifications.

documents.name: Third-Party Data-Sharing Register
documents.description: Central register recording each data-sharing operation, the third party involved, data scope, purpose, justification, owner, and relevant dates.

documents.name: Data-Sharing Request and Approval Form
documents.description: Form used to capture the proposed sharing activity and its justification before or at the time of authorization.

documents.name: Third-Party Data Flow Inventory
documents.description: Inventory showing data flows between the organization and third parties, linked to the corresponding sharing records.

documents.name: Data-Sharing Review Procedure
documents.description: Procedure for creating, updating, periodically reviewing, and closing data-sharing records.

evidence.name: Completed data-sharing register entries
evidence.description: Current records showing third-party sharing operations and the justification for each activity.

evidence.name: Approved data-sharing requests
evidence.description: Requests or approvals that document why the data was shared and who authorized the activity.

evidence.name: Data flow diagrams or inventories
evidence.description: Artifacts corroborating the third-party data exchanges recorded in the register.

evidence.name: Periodic register review records
evidence.description: Evidence that data-sharing records are reviewed and kept current.

requirements.source_text: 3-1-1-4When transferring data outside the kingdom, the capability of the hosting organization abroad to safeguard data must be verified, approval ofthe Authorizing Officialmust be obtained and complyingwith related laws and regulations.
requirements.source_summary: Before transferring data outside the kingdom, the organization must verify the overseas host’s ability to safeguard the data, obtain Authorizing Official approval, and comply with applicable laws and regulations.

todo.name: Control transfers of data outside the kingdom
todo.description: Implement a pre-transfer assessment and approval workflow that evaluates the overseas hosting organization’s safeguards, records applicable legal and regulatory considerations, obtains Authorizing Official approval, and prevents transfer until requirements are satisfied.

policies.name: Cross-Border Data Transfer Policy
policies.description: Define conditions, assessment criteria, approval steps, and compliance checks for transferring data to hosting organizations outside the kingdom.

policies.name: Third-Party Security Assessment Policy
policies.description: Require evaluation of an overseas hosting organization’s capability to safeguard organizational data before transfer.

policies.name: Data Transfer Authorization Policy
policies.description: Establish the Authority and process for obtaining and recording Authorizing Official approval.

documents.name: Cross-Border Data Transfer Assessment
documents.description: Assessment documenting the overseas host, data involved, safeguards reviewed, findings, and compliance considerations.

documents.name: Authorizing Official Approval Record
documents.description: Formal approval record tied to the specific proposed transfer and its supporting assessment.

documents.name: Cross-Border Data Transfer Register
documents.description: Register of approved transfers, destinations, hosting organizations, data scope, approval status, and review dates.

documents.name: Legal and Regulatory Compliance Checklist
documents.description: Checklist for recording the applicable laws and regulations considered for each proposed transfer.

documents.name: Overseas Hosting Organization Due-Diligence Questionnaire
documents.description: Questionnaire and supporting review materials used to assess the host’s capability to safeguard data.

evidence.name: Completed overseas host security assessments
evidence.description: Assessments showing that the hosting organization’s safeguards were evaluated before transfer.

evidence.name: Authorizing Official approvals
evidence.description: Documented approvals for the relevant transfers, linked to the assessment and transfer scope.

evidence.name: Cross-border transfer register
evidence.description: Current register demonstrating that transfers are tracked and their authorization status is known.

evidence.name: Legal and regulatory review records
evidence.description: Completed checklists or legal reviews showing consideration of applicable laws and regulations.

evidence.name: Contractual and technical safeguard records
evidence.description: Relevant agreements and technical control documentation supporting the overseas host’s ability to safeguard the transferred data.

requirements.source_text: 3-1-1-5Requiring third-parties to notify the organization immediately in case of cybersecurity incident that may affect data that has been shared or created.
requirements.source_summary: Third parties must notify the organization immediately when a cybersecurity incident may affect data that was shared with them or created by them.

todo.name: Implement immediate third-party incident notification
todo.description: Add an immediate notification obligation to third-party arrangements, define the notification channels and required incident information, and establish an internal process to receive, escalate, assess, and respond to notifications affecting shared or third-party-created data.

policies.name: Third-Party Cybersecurity Incident Management Policy
policies.description: Define third-party notification expectations, internal escalation, incident ownership, and coordination when shared or third-party-created data may be affected.

policies.name: Incident Notification and Escalation Policy
policies.description: Specify approved notification channels, responsible contacts, escalation paths, and handling requirements for urgent third-party incident reports.

documents.name: Third-Party Incident Notification Clause
documents.description: Contractual provision requiring immediate notification of cybersecurity incidents that may affect relevant organizational data.

documents.name: Third-Party Incident Response Procedure
documents.description: Procedure for receiving, validating, escalating, documenting, and responding to incident notifications from third parties.

documents.name: Third-Party Contact and Escalation Register
documents.description: Maintained list of third-party incident contacts, alternates, organizational owners, and escalation routes.

documents.name: Third-Party Incident Log
documents.description: Record of notifications received, affected data, actions taken, communications, and closure status.

documents.name: Third-Party Incident Notification Form
documents.description: Standard form for capturing the initial incident details and subsequent updates from a third party.

evidence.name: Executed third-party agreements
evidence.description: Contracts containing the immediate incident notification obligation and relevant contact details.

evidence.name: Incident notification records
evidence.description: Examples of third-party notifications and the organization’s documented response and escalation.

evidence.name: Third-party contact testing records
evidence.description: Records of contact validation or exercises demonstrating that notification channels can be used.

evidence.name: Incident logs and communications
evidence.description: Ticketing, case-management, or communication records showing tracking of affected shared or created data.

requirements.source_text: 3-1-1-6Reclassifying data to the least level to achieve the objective before sharing it with third-parties using data masking or data scrambling techniques.
requirements.source_summary: Before sharing data with third parties, the data must be reclassified to the least level needed for the objective, using masking or scrambling techniques.

todo.name: Minimize and protect data before third-party sharing
todo.description: Add a pre-sharing review that determines the minimum classification level needed for the intended objective and applies approved masking or scrambling techniques before release, with the result documented and verified.

policies.name: Third-Party Data Minimization Policy
policies.description: Require the organization to limit data shared with third parties to the least classification level needed for the stated objective.

policies.name: Data Masking and Scrambling Policy
policies.description: Define approved techniques, responsibilities, validation steps, and exceptions for masking or scrambling data before third-party sharing.

policies.name: Data Classification Policy
policies.description: Define classification and reclassification responsibilities for data prepared for external sharing.

documents.name: Third-Party Data-Sharing Assessment
documents.description: Assessment documenting the sharing objective, data required, minimum classification level, and protection techniques applied.

documents.name: Data Masking and Scrambling Procedure
documents.description: Procedure for selecting, applying, validating, and recording masking or scrambling before data is shared.

documents.name: Data Transformation and Release Record
documents.description: Record identifying the source data, transformed dataset, technique used, reviewer, approval, and release date.

documents.name: Approved Masking and Scrambling Standards
documents.description: Technical standards describing approved methods and validation criteria for protecting data before release.

documents.name: Third-Party Data-Sharing Register
documents.description: Register linking each sharing operation to its minimization, reclassification, and transformation records.

evidence.name: Pre-sharing assessment records
evidence.description: Completed reviews showing that the minimum necessary classification level was determined for the sharing objective.

evidence.name: Masked or scrambled sample datasets
evidence.description: Representative outputs demonstrating that protection techniques were applied before third-party release.

evidence.name: Transformation and quality-validation logs
evidence.description: Technical or operational records showing the data transformation performed and its verification.

evidence.name: Approved data release records
evidence.description: Authorizations or release records linking the protected dataset to the intended third-party sharing activity.

evidence.name: Data classification review records
evidence.description: Records showing the data was reviewed and reclassified before sharing where applicable.
